1.explanation: The Sort component (in src/table/base/sort.jsx) is responsible for rendering the sort icons inside a <span> with role="button". Its renderSort method does not apply any cursor styling, so hover still shows the default cursor. To fix this, you should add a ‘cursor: pointer’ style (either inline or via the CSS class `${prefix}table-sort`) in renderSort, ensuring users see the pointer cursor over the sort icons and understand they are clickable.
1.bug_scenario: In the Table component example on the documentation site, the sort icons rendered next to the column header (e.g. “Id” column) do not show a pointer cursor on hover. Users see the default arrow cursor when hovering over the clickable sort arrows, making it unclear that the icons are interactive.

2.explanation: The Sort component (in src/table/base/sort.jsx) renders the sort UI inside the renderSort() method by returning a <span> that acts as the clickable area for sorting. This wrapper has role="button" and handles click/keyboard events, but no cursor style is applied, so the cursor remains default when hovering over it. To fix the bug, renderSort() should add cursor: 'pointer' to the <span> (either via inline style or via the CSS class `${prefix}table-sort`) so users see the pointer cursor and know the element is interactive.
2.bug_scenario: In the Table component’s header, the sort icons (up/down arrows) are wrapped in a <span> with role="button" but do not show a pointer cursor on hover. Users expect the cursor to change to indicate the area is clickable (e.g. cursor: pointer), but currently it remains the default text cursor when hovering between the icons or on the wrapper area.
